# APEX OMNI VAULT — MASTER SLAB

## PURPOSE
Omni Vault is the unified secret management layer for the entire APEX ecosystem. It provides a single interface for retrieving, rotating, validating, and auditing secrets across all environments (local, dev, staging, production). No service may store secrets locally or embed them in code.

---

## CORE PRINCIPLES
- Secrets NEVER live in code or commits.
- Secrets ALWAYS load at runtime from a secure backend.
- Startup MUST fail if any required secret is missing.
- Provider-agnostic: GCP, AWS, HashiCorp Vault supported.
- Rotation is mandatory for production.
- Audit logs required for every secret access.
- Least-privilege access enforced across all services.

---

## DIRECTORY STRUCTURE

---

## REQUIRED SECRETS (GLOBAL)
Every APEX service must retrieve these via Omni Vault:

### Infrastructure
- DATABASE_URL  
- REDIS_URL  
- TEMPORAL_URL  

### Security
- JWT_SECRET  
- GATEKEEPER_PRIVATE_KEY  
- STEWART_POLICY_KEY  
- SENTINEL_API_KEY  

### AI
- OPENAI_API_KEY  
- GOOGLE_API_KEY  

### Payments
- STRIPE_SECRET_KEY  
- STRIPE_CONNECT_KEY  
- STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET  

### Integrations
- SHOPIFY_API_KEY  
- SHOPIFY_API_SECRET  
- SHOPIFY_STORE_URL  
- CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY  
- CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID  
- GITHUB_TOKEN  

### Storage
- SUPABASE_URL  
- SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY  

---

## STARTUP CONTRACT (MANDATORY)
Every service using Omni Vault MUST:

1. Request all required secrets at startup.
2. Abort immediately if ANY secret is missing.
3. Log a structured error:
   - service name  
   - missing secret  
   - environment  
   - timestamp  
4. Expose `/health`, `/ready`, `/metrics` reflecting vault status.
5. Deny all requests until vault validation passes.

This is non-negotiable.

---

## PROVIDER REQUIREMENTS
### GCP Secret Manager
- IAM role: `secretAccessor`
- Service account required
- Audit logs enabled
- Versioned secrets mandatory

### AWS Secrets Manager
- IAM policy: least privilege
- Automatic rotation supported
- CloudTrail logging required

### HashiCorp Vault
- Token or AppRole auth
- Dynamic secrets preferred
- Lease renewal required

---

## LOCAL DEVELOPMENT RULES
Local `.env` usage is allowed ONLY when:

- `OMNI_VAULT_ENV=local`
- `.env` file exists in `/local`
- No production keys are present
- Local secrets NEVER commit to Git

---

## ROTATION POLICY
Rotation must occur:

- Every 30 days (time-based)
- After any security incident (event-based)
- After any provider credential change
- After any environment migration

Rotation logs MUST include:

- old version  
- new version  
- rotation actor  
- timestamp  
- affected services  

---

## TESTING REQUIREMENTS
### Unit Tests
- Provider mocks
- Secret retrieval
- Missing secret failure

### Integration Tests
- Real provider access
- Rotation workflow
- Startup contract enforcement

### CI/CD Gates
- Vault tests MUST pass
- No merge allowed if vault fails
- No deploy allowed if vault fails

---

## SECURITY RULES
- `.env` files NEVER commit.
- GitHub Actions NEVER store plaintext secrets.
- External links MUST use:
  - `target="_blank"`
  - `rel="noopener noreferrer"`
- AI-generated URLs MUST be sanitized before rendering.
- All vault errors MUST be structured and logged.

ExpansionI’ll make a few explicit assumptions, then give you a buildable monorepo with full configs and entrypoints, grouped by layer and in the order you should create files.

---

Assumptions

• Runtime: Node.js ^20, TypeScript ^5.
• Framework: Minimal REST using express.
• Monorepo: npm workspaces, root package.json manages all services and shared libs.
• Env: .env per service, .env.example at root.
• Local infra: Docker Compose runs Postgres, Redis, and all services.
• Temporal: Used via HTTP API (no custom worker code here, just a client stub).

version: "3.9"

services:

    image: postgres:16

      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: apexpassword

      - redis

    build: ./services/phoenix
    env_file: .env
    ports:
      - "${PHOENIX_PORT}:4002"
    depends_on:
      - postgres
      - redis
      - bifrost
      - vault
      - stewart

  bifrost:
    build: ./services/bifrost-gateway

    ports:

`packages/shared-config/src/config.ts`

import dotenv from "dotenv";

dotenv.config();

export interface ServiceConfig {
  port: number;
  postgresUrl: string;
  redisHost: string;
  redisPort: number;
  nodeEnv: string;
}

export function loadServiceConfig(portEnvVar: string): ServiceConfig {
  const nodeEnv = process.env.NODE_ENV || "development";

  const port = Number(process.env[portEnvVar] || 0);
  if (!port) {
    throw new Error(`Missing or invalid port env var: ${portEnvVar}`);
  }

  const postgresUrl =
    process.env.POSTGRES_URL ||
    `postgres://apex:apexpassword@postgres:5432/apexdb`;

  const redisHost = process.env.REDIS_HOST || "redis";
  const redisPort = Number(process.env.REDIS_PORT || 6379);

  return {
    port,
    postgresUrl,
    redisHost,
    redisPort,
    nodeEnv
  };
}

export type LogLevel = "debug" | "info" | "warn" | "error";

export class Logger {
  constructor(private readonly serviceName: string) {}

  private log(level: LogLevel, message: string, meta?: unknown) {
    const payload = {
      service: this.serviceName,
      level,
      message,
      meta,
      timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
    };
    // For now, console; later, send to Sentinel.
    console.log(JSON.stringify(payload));
  }

  debug(message: string, meta?: unknown) {
    this.log("debug", message, meta);
  }

  info(message: string, meta?: unknown) {
    this.log("info", message, meta);
  }

  warn(message: string, meta?: unknown) {
    this.log("warn", message, meta);
  }

  error(message: string, meta?: unknown) {
    this.log("error", message, meta);
  }
}

import express, { Express } from "express";
import cors from "cors";

export function createServer(): Express {
  const app = express();

  app.use(cors());
  app.use(express.json());

  return app;
}


`packages/shared-http/src/errorHandler.ts`

import { Request, Response, NextFunction } from "express";

export function errorHandler(
  err: unknown,
  _req: Request,
  res: Response,
  _next: NextFunction
) {
  const status = 500;
  const message =
    err instanceof Error ? err.message : "Internal server error";

  res.status(status).json({ error: message });
}

2.2 One‑sentence explanations (infra services)

• APEX Bridge — Integrates with external APIs (Stripe, Shopify, Cloudflare, GitHub) and exposes internal REST endpoints.
• Phoenix — Main backend orchestrator coordinating Customer Success flows and calling Bridge, Stewart, Temporal, and Omni Vault.
• Bifrost Gateway — API gateway routing external client requests to Phoenix and other internal services.
• Omni Vault — Secrets/config service providing runtime configuration to all services.
• Stewart — Authentication and identity service issuing and validating JWTs.
• Sentinel — Monitoring and alerting service receiving logs/metrics and exposing health endpoints.
• Temporal Client — Thin REST client that triggers and inspects Temporal workflows.

2.3 Service‑level configs and entrypoints

Common Dockerfile pattern (each service)

Example for services/apex-bridge/Dockerfile (repeat with appropriate context path):

FROM node:20-alpine

WORKDIR /usr/src/app

COPY package.json tsconfig.json ./
COPY ../../packages ./packages
COPY src ./src

RUN npm install --omit=dev
RUN npx tsc -p tsconfig.json

CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]


For brevity, use the same pattern for all services, adjusting COPY paths if needed; in practice you might build from root and use npm ci with workspaces.

import { createServer } from "@apex/shared-http";
import { errorHandler } from "@apex/shared-http/dist/errorHandler";
import { loadServiceConfig } from "@apex/shared-config";
import { Logger } from "@apex/shared-logger";
import axios from "axios";

const logger = new Logger("apex-bridge");
const config = loadServiceConfig("BRIDGE_PORT");
const app = createServer();

// Simple health endpoint
app.get("/health", (_req, res) => {
  res.json({ status: "ok", service: "apex-bridge" });
});

// Example Stripe proxy
app.post("/bridge/stripe/charge", async (req, res, next) => {
  try {
    const stripeKey = process.env.STRIPE_API_KEY;
    if (!stripeKey) {
      throw new Error("Missing STRIPE_API_KEY");
    }

    // Placeholder: call Stripe API
    logger.info("Stripe charge requested", { body: req.body });
    res.json({ ok: true });
  } catch (err) {
    logger.error("Stripe charge failed", err);
    next(err);
  }
});

app.use(errorHandler);

app.listen(config.port, () => {
  logger.info(`APEX Bridge listening on port ${config.port}`);
});

`services/phoenix/src/index.ts`

import { createServer } from "@apex/shared-http";
import { errorHandler } from "@apex/shared-http/dist/errorHandler";
import { loadServiceConfig } from "@apex/shared-config";
import { Logger } from "@apex/shared-logger";
import axios from "axios";

const logger = new Logger("phoenix");
const config = loadServiceConfig("PHOENIX_PORT");
const app = createServer();

// Health
app.get("/health", (_req, res) => {
  res.json({ status: "ok", service: "phoenix" });
});

// Example orchestrated customer success flow
app.post("/customer-success/ticket", async (req, res, next) => {
  try {
    logger.info("New ticket received", { body: req.body });

    // Call Stewart for auth check
    const authHeader = req.headers.authorization;
    if (!authHeader) {
      return res.status(401).json({ error: "Missing Authorization header" });
    }

    await axios.post(`${process.env.STEWART_URL}/auth/validate`, null, {
      headers: { Authorization: authHeader }
    });

    // Call Bridge for external integration (e.g., Stripe)
    await axios.post(`${process.env.BRIDGE_URL}/bridge/stripe/charge`, {
      amount: req.body.amount,
      customerId: req.body.customerId
    });

    // Call Temporal client to start workflow
    await axios.post(`${process.env.TEMPORAL_CLIENT_URL}/workflow/start`, {
      type: "ticket-resolution",
      payload: req.body
    });

    res.json({ ok: true });
  } catch (err) {
    logger.error("Ticket flow failed", err);
    next(err);
  }
});

app.use(errorHandler);

app.listen(config.port, () => {
  logger.info(`Phoenix listening on port ${config.port}`);
});

import { createServer } from "@apex/shared-http";
import { errorHandler } from "@apex/shared-http/dist/errorHandler";
import { loadServiceConfig } from "@apex/shared-config";
import { Logger } from "@apex/shared-logger";
import { createProxyMiddleware } from "http-proxy-middleware";

const logger = new Logger("bifrost-gateway");
const config = loadServiceConfig("BIFROST_PORT");
const app = createServer();

// Health
app.get("/health", (_req, res) => {
  res.json({ status: "ok", service: "bifrost-gateway" });
});

// Route external clients to Phoenix
app.use(
  "/api",
  createProxyMiddleware({
    target: process.env.PHOENIX_URL || "http://phoenix:4002",
    changeOrigin: true,
    pathRewrite: { "^/api": "" }
  })
);

app.use(errorHandler);

app.listen(config.port, () => {
  logger.info(`Bifrost Gateway listening on port ${config.port}`);
});

import { createServer } from "@apex/shared-http";
import { errorHandler } from "@apex/shared-http/dist/errorHandler";
import { loadServiceConfig } from "@apex/shared-config";
import { Logger } from "@apex/shared-logger";
import jwt from "jsonwebtoken";

const logger = new Logger("stewart");
const config = loadServiceConfig("STEWART_PORT");
const app = createServer();

const JWT_SECRET = process.env.JWT_SECRET || "supersecretjwt";

app.get("/health", (_req, res) => {
  res.json({ status: "ok", service: "stewart" });
});

app.post("/auth/login", (req, res) => {
  const { userId } = req.body;
  if (!userId) {
    return res.status(400).json({ error: "Missing userId" });
  }
  const token = jwt.sign({ sub: userId }, JWT_SECRET, { expiresIn: "1h" });
  res.json({ token });
});

app.post("/auth/validate", (req, res) => {
  const auth = req.headers.authorization;
  if (!auth?.startsWith("Bearer ")) {
    return res.status(401).json({ error: "Invalid Authorization header" });
  }
  const token = auth.slice("Bearer ".length);
  try {
    const payload = jwt.verify(token, JWT_SECRET);
    res.json({ valid: true, payload });
  } catch (err) {
    logger.warn("Token validation failed", err);
    res.status(401).json({ error: "Invalid token" });
  }
});

app.use(errorHandler);

app.listen(config.port, () => {
  logger.info(`Stewart listening on port ${config.port}`);
});

Layer 3 — Placement & creation order

3.1 Relative placement

• Project root: apex-platform/• Contains root package.json, tsconfig.base.json, tsconfig.json, .gitignore, .env.example, docker-compose.yml, README.md.

• Shared libs: apex-platform/packages/…• shared-config, shared-logger, shared-http.

• Services: apex-platform/services/…• apex-bridge, phoenix, bifrost-gateway, omni-vault, stewart-auth, sentinel-monitor, temporal-client.



3.2 Creation order (step‑by‑step)

1. Create project root: apex-platform/.
2. Add root files: package.json, tsconfig.base.json, tsconfig.json, .gitignore, .env.example, docker-compose.yml, README.md.
3. Create packages/ directory.
4. Create packages/shared-config with its package.json, tsconfig.json, src/config.ts.
5. Create packages/shared-logger with its package.json, tsconfig.json, src/logger.ts.
6. Create packages/shared-http with its package.json, tsconfig.json, src/createServer.ts, src/errorHandler.ts.
7. Create services/ directory.
8. For each service (apex-bridge, phoenix, bifrost-gateway, omni-vault, stewart-auth, sentinel-monitor, temporal-client):• Create folder under services/.
• Add package.json, tsconfig.json, .env.example, Dockerfile, src/index.ts.

9. Run npm install at root to wire workspaces.
10. Run npm run build:packages then npm run build:services.
11. Run npm run dev (Docker Compose) to bring up the full stack.

# Omni Vault

Omni Vault is the unified secret/config service for the APEX platform.

- Provides runtime secrets to Phoenix, Bridge, Stewart, Sentinel, etc.
- Supports multiple backends (local, GCP, AWS, HashiCorp Vault).
- Enforces fail-fast startup if required secrets are missing.
- Exposes REST endpoints for secret retrieval and health checks.
export type VaultBackendType = "local" | "gcp" | "aws" | "hashicorp";

export interface SecretRecord {
  key: string;
  value: string;
}

export interface VaultClient {
  getSecret(key: string): Promise<string | null>;
  listSecrets(): Promise<SecretRecord[]>;
}
import fs from "fs";
import path from "path";
import { VaultBackendType, VaultClient, SecretRecord } from "./types";

class LocalVaultClient implements VaultClient {
  private secrets: Record<string, string> = {};

  constructor(localFilePath: string) {
    const fullPath = path.resolve(localFilePath);
    if (fs.existsSync(fullPath)) {
      const raw = fs.readFileSync(fullPath, "utf-8");
      this.secrets = JSON.parse(raw);
    }
  }

  async getSecret(key: string): Promise<string | null> {
    return this.secrets[key] ?? null;
  }

  async listSecrets(): Promise<SecretRecord[]> {
    return Object.entries(this.secrets).map(([key, value]) => ({ key, value }));
  }
}

// Placeholder stubs for future backends
class GcpVaultClient implements VaultClient {
  async getSecret(_key: string): Promise<string | null> {
    throw new Error("GCP backend not implemented");
  }
  async listSecrets(): Promise<SecretRecord[]> {
    throw new Error("GCP backend not implemented");
  }
}

class AwsVaultClient implements VaultClient {
  async getSecret(_key: string): Promise<string | null> {
    throw new Error("AWS backend not implemented");
  }
  async listSecrets(): Promise<SecretRecord[]> {
    throw new Error("AWS backend not implemented");
  }
}

class HashicorpVaultClient implements VaultClient {
  async getSecret(_key: string): Promise<string | null> {
    throw new Error("Hashicorp backend not implemented");
  }
  async listSecrets(): Promise<SecretRecord[]> {
    throw new Error("Hashicorp backend not implemented");
  }
}

export function createVaultClient(): VaultClient {
  const backend = (process.env.VAULT_BACKEND || "local") as VaultBackendType;

  switch (backend) {
    case "local": {
      const file = process.env.VAULT_LOCAL_FILE || "./local-secrets.json";
      return new LocalVaultClient(file);
    }
    case "gcp":
      return new GcpVaultClient();
    case "aws":
      return new AwsVaultClient();
    case "hashicorp":
      return new HashicorpVaultClient();
    default:
      throw new Error(`Unsupported VAULT_BACKEND: ${backend}`);
  }
}
import { Router } from "express";

export function healthRouter() {
  const router = Router();

  router.get("/health", (_req, res) => {
    res.json({ status: "ok", service: "omni-vault" });
  });

  return router;
}
import { Router } from "express";
import { VaultClient } from "../core/types";

export function secretsRouter(vaultClient: VaultClient) {
  const router = Router();

  router.get("/secrets", async (_req, res, next) => {
    try {
      const secrets = await vaultClient.listSecrets();
      res.json({ secrets });
    } catch (err) {
      next(err);
    }
  });

  router.get("/secrets/:key", async (req, res, next) => {
    try {
      const key = req.params.key;
      const value = await vaultClient.getSecret(key);
      if (!value) {
        return res.status(404).json({ error: "Secret not found" });
      }
      res.json({ key, value });
    } catch (err) {
      next(err);
    }
  });

  return router;
}
import { createServer } from "@apex/shared-http";
import { errorHandler } from "@apex/shared-http/dist/errorHandler";
import { loadServiceConfig } from "@apex/shared-config";
import { Logger } from "@apex/shared-logger";
import { createVaultClient } from "./core/vaultClient";
import { healthRouter } from "./routes/health";
import { secretsRouter } from "./routes/secrets";

const logger = new Logger("omni-vault");
const config = loadServiceConfig("VAULT_PORT");
const app = createServer();

const vaultClient = createVaultClient();

// Routes
app.use(healthRouter());
app.use(secretsRouter(vaultClient));

// Error handler
app.use(errorHandler);

// Startup
app.listen(config.port, () => {
  logger.info(`Omni Vault listening on port ${config.port}`);
});
const vaultUrl = process.env.VAULT_URL || "http://vault:4004";

const stripeKey = await axios
  .get(`${vaultUrl}/secrets/STRIPE_API_KEY`)
  .then((r) => r.data.value);

    return this.secrets[key] ?? null;
  }

  async listSecrets(): Promise<SecretRecord[]> {
    return Object.entries(this.secrets).map(([key, value]) => ({ key, value }));
  }
}

export function createVaultClient(): VaultClient {
  const backend = (process.env.VAULT_BACKEND || "local") as VaultBackendType;

  switch (backend) {
    case "local": {
      const file = process.env.VAULT_LOCAL_FILE || "./local-secrets.json";
      return new LocalVaultClient(file);
    }
    case "gcp":
      return new GcpVaultClient();
    case "aws":
      return new AwsVaultClient();
    case "hashicorp":
      return new HashicorpVaultClient();
    default:
      throw new Error(`Unsupported VAULT_BACKEND: ${backend}`);
  }
}
import { Router } from "express";

export function healthRouter() {
  const router = Router();

import { Router } from "express";
import { VaultClient } from "../core/types";

export function secretsRouter(vaultClient: VaultClient) {
  const router = Router();

  router.get("/secrets", async (_req, res, next) => {
    try {
      const secrets = await vaultClient.listSecrets();
      res.json({ secrets });
    } catch (err) {
      next(err);
    }
  });

  router.get("/secrets/:key", async (req, res, next) => {
    try {
      const key = req.params.key;
      const value = await vaultClient.getSecret(key);
      if (!value) {
        return res.status(404).json({ error: "Secret not found" });
      }
      res.json({ key, value });
    } catch (err) {
      next(err);
    }
  });

  return router;
}

Yes. If your goal is “everything only to make Omni Vault work”, then I’d temporarily treat Omni Vault as the center of the platform and make every other component support it.

Phase 1: Omni Vault First

Build order

1. Omni Vault
    * Secret providers
    * Runtime validation
    * Rotation
    * Audit logging
    * /health
    * /ready
    * /metrics
2. Stewart
    * Authentication
    * Authorization
    * JWT signing
    * Policy enforcement
    * Uses Omni Vault for all secrets
3. Gateway
    * Request validation
    * API routing
    * Rate limiting
    * Retrieves configuration from Omni Vault
4. Phoenix
    * Workflow orchestration
    * Never stores secrets
    * Requests all configuration from Omni Vault
5. Sentinel
    * Monitoring
    * Metrics
    * Audit ingestion
    * Watches Omni Vault health
6. Terminal
    * Operations console
    * Rotation commands
    * Secret validation
    * Diagnostics
7. Bridge
    * Public interface
    * Calls Gateway only
    * Never accesses secrets directly

Non-negotiable rule

Every service must:

* Start by connecting to Omni Vault.
* Validate required secrets.
* Refuse to serve requests if validation fails.
* Never hardcode API keys, passwords, or tokens.
* Expose health endpoints that reflect Vault status.

Single source of truth

If Omni Vault is the foundation, then every component depends on it:

* Phoenix → Omni Vault
* Gateway → Omni Vault
* Stewart → Omni Vault
* Sentinel → Omni Vault
* Terminal → Omni Vault
* Bridge → Gateway → Omni Vault

That makes Omni Vault the trust root for the platform while APEX Bridge remains the public front door. This separation keeps secret management centralized without exposing it directly to users.

---

🟩 APEX GATEWAY — MASTER SLAB (Omni Vault‑First Architecture)

PURPOSE

APEX Gateway is the API gateway and request‑routing layer. It is the internal ingress for all service‑to‑service communication. It depends on Omni Vault for runtime configuration, routing rules, and secret‑free operation. External client traffic enters through APEX Bridge and is forwarded here; Gateway never exposes itself to the public internet directly.

---

CORE PRINCIPLES

· All configuration comes from Omni Vault at startup.
· Zero hardcoded API keys, tokens, or passwords.
· Startup fails immediately if Omni Vault is unreachable or required secrets are missing.
· Rate limiting, request validation, and route mapping are defined by Vault‑sourced policies.
· Gateway exposes /health, /ready, /metrics, with Vault‑connectivity status.
· Every route is dynamically loaded from Omni Vault config.

---

DIRECTORY STRUCTURE (inside monorepo services/bifrost-gateway)

bifrost-gateway/ ├── src/ │   ├── index.ts          # Entry point, Vault connection, route loading │   ├── routes/           # Dynamic route configuration pulled from Vault │   ├── middleware/        # Auth, rate limiting, logging │   └── vault-client.ts   # Dedicated client for Omni Vault ├── package.json ├── tsconfig.json ├── .env.example ├── Dockerfile └── README.md

---

STARTUP CONTRACT (MANDATORY, Omni Vault‑aware)

1. On startup, connect to Omni Vault using VAULT_URL.
2. Request GATEWAY_CONFIG secret (a JSON blob containing routes, rate‑limit policies, upstream URLs).
3. Validate mandatory fields: routes, upstreams, globalRateLimit.
4. If Vault is unreachable, retry 3 times with backoff; if still failing, exit with code 1 and log structured error.
5. Once configuration is loaded, build proxy table and start HTTP server.
6. Expose /health and /ready endpoints:
   · /health returns vault status, uptime.
   · /ready returns true only if Vault config is loaded and all required upstreams are reachable (health‑check pings).
7. Any secret refresh (via Vault watch) must update routes without downtime.

---

REQUIRED SECRETS FROM OMNI VAULT

Gateway fetches these from Vault at runtime:

Secret Name Purpose
GATEWAY_CONFIG Full routing & policy configuration
GATEWAY_JWT_PUBLIC_KEY Public key for validating JWTs from Stewart
GATEWAY_RATE_LIMIT_REDIS_URL Redis connection string for distributed rate limiting
GATEWAY_SERVICE_REGISTRY Map of service names to internal URLs (Phoenix, Bridge, Stewart, etc.)

No other secrets are stored locally.

---

ROUTING CONFIGURATION SCHEMA (stored in GATEWAY_CONFIG secret)

```json
{
  "routes": [
    {
      "path": "/api/*",
      "upstream": "phoenix",
      "methods": ["GET","POST","PUT","DELETE"],
      "authRequired": true
    },
    {
      "path": "/auth/*",
      "upstream": "stewart",
      "methods": ["POST"],
      "authRequired": false
    }
  ],
  "globalRateLimit": {
    "windowMs": 60000,
    "max": 1000
  },
  "upstreams": {
    "phoenix": "http://phoenix:4002",
    "stewart": "http://stewart:4005",
    "bridge": "http://bridge:4001"
  }
}
```

Gateway parses this and creates proxy middleware dynamically.

---

RATE LIMITING & SECURITY

· Rate limiting uses Redis, connection string from GATEWAY_RATE_LIMIT_REDIS_URL.
· JWT validation middleware uses the public key from GATEWAY_JWT_PUBLIC_KEY to verify tokens signed by Stewart. No private key ever touches Gateway.
· All inbound requests are validated against route definitions; unmatched routes return 404.
· CORS is handled at the Bridge layer; Gateway assumes internal traffic only.

---

AUDIT & LOGGING

· Every request logs: timestamp, method, path, upstream service, response status, latency.
· Structured JSON logs sent to stdout (collected by Sentinel later).
· Audit events (config reload, Vault connection loss) logged with severity warn or error.

---

CI/CD GATES (Vault‑dependent)

· Gateway integration tests must spin up a mock Omni Vault and verify startup sequence.
· No merge allowed if Vault integration test fails.
· No deploy allowed if Gateway cannot retrieve and apply GATEWAY_CONFIG from staging/production Vault.

---

DEPENDENCY GRAPH

· Omni Vault (runtime config)
· Stewart (auth token validation)
· Phoenix, Bridge (upstream services)

Gateway is a consumer of Omni Vault and Stewart; it depends on both being healthy.

---

OPERATIONAL COMMANDS (via Terminal slab – later)

· gateway:reload – force reload of Vault config without restart.
· gateway:routes – list active routes and their status.
· gateway:health – detailed connectivity report including Vault and upstreams.

---
